events.title: The Battle of Bunker Hill
events.description: British forces attacked American colonial positions on the heights above Boston. They took the ground, but only after suffering heavy losses against determined militia.
events.significance: The battle showed that colonial fighters could stand up to professional British troops. It hardened both sides in the American Revolutionary War.

events.title: The Statue of Liberty Arrives in New York
events.description: The French ship Isère delivered the Statue of Liberty to New York Harbor. It came in 350 pieces packed into more than 200 crates.
events.significance: The gift from France was later assembled on its pedestal and became a global symbol of freedom and welcome.

events.title: Iceland Becomes a Republic
events.description: Iceland formally declared itself a republic and ended its union with the Danish crown. The declaration came at a ceremony at Þingvellir.
events.significance: Independence completed Iceland's long path to self-rule. The nation chose the date to honor the birthday of independence leader Jón Sigurðsson.

events.title: The Watergate Break-In Arrests
events.description: Five men were arrested while trying to bug the Democratic National Committee offices at the Watergate complex in Washington, D.C. The burglars were tied to President Nixon's re-election effort.
events.significance: The arrests set off the Watergate scandal. It ended in 1974 with Richard Nixon's resignation and left lasting changes in how Americans view government accountability.

events.title: Birth of Venus Williams
events.description: Tennis champion Venus Williams was born. She rose to the top of the sport and won multiple Grand Slam singles titles.
events.significance: Williams helped transform modern women's tennis with her power and her advocacy for equal prize money at Wimbledon.
